nina: quick sync - we need a final call on SDK defaults: prefetch ownership, transport negotiation, and resume-token semantics across py/ts/go.

ethan: proposal: unary-by-default, optional session stream for long-lived flows. SDKs expose same config but default resolves by deployment metadata.

lee: agree on unary default. for resume tokens: keep them opaque but stable, include server-side monotonic offsets so retry/resume is safe.

mina: who handles prefetch backoff? component that issues the prefetch should own it. server-prefetch uses server limits; sdk should implement idempotent cancel/resume.

nina: how do we avoid double-prefetch when old SDK talks to new server? add a small capability header like `x-rw-prefetch: v1` so client-side prefetch can skip.

ethan: add negotiation header `x-rw-session: stream=1,prefetch=1,ver=1` so SDKs know whether to open control stream. fallback to unary if missing.

lee: iterator ergonomics: provide high-level iterator that hides retry/resume. on stale cursor error return resume_token in error payload so SDK auto-resumes.

mina: billing note: speculative prefetch tokens should be billable only if consumed. add telemetry labels `prefetch_speculative` and `transport_mode`. keep conservative default window=96 tokens.

nina: short-term decisions: unary default + opt-in session stream, capability header, resume-token error shape, conservative window. long-term: unify prefetch+kv-cache into cache policy module.

ethan: i'll sketch RFC and test matrix (old-sdk/new-server combos).

infra-bot: created issue INFR-3099: "sdk-prefetch-transport-resume-interop" assigned to @ethan.

nina: thanks all, i'll close this thread and collect RFC feedback. :handshake:
